requirements.text: Record all FLEX Option purchases, sales, writes and closing transactions on trade date.
requirements.source: “Investment transactions are recorded on the trade date.”

requirements.text: For each purchased option, record the premium paid as an investment at identified cost and subsequently remeasure it to current value; treat purchased options as non-income-producing investments.
requirements.source: “When the Funds purchase an option, an amount equal to the premium paid by the Funds are recorded as an investment and is subsequently adjusted to the current value of the option purchased.”

requirements.text: For each written option, record the premium received as a liability and subsequently remeasure the liability to current value.
requirements.source: “When the Funds write an option, an amount equal to the premium received by the Funds are recorded as a liability and is subsequently adjusted to the current value of the option written.”

requirements.text: Maintain each option's reference asset, call or put designation, purchased or written designation, strike, expiration date, European exercise style, cash-settlement terms, contract quantity and multiplier; use 100 reference shares per contract unless adjusted by the exchange or OCC.
requirements.source: “The FLEX Options in which the Fund invests are all European style option contracts”; “All of the FLEX Option contracts held by the Funds are fully funded and cash settled”; “100 shares per contract.”

requirements.text: Do not offset purchased-option assets against written-option liabilities on the balance sheet.
requirements.source: “All of the FLEX Option contracts held by the Funds are fully funded and cash settled, therefore balance sheet offsetting under U.S. GAAP does not apply.”

requirements.text: Each NYSE business day, value the FLEX Options as of the applicable NAV calculation time, ordinarily the NYSE close at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time or the actual early close.
requirements.source: “USBFS…calculates the Fund’s NAV at the close of regular trading (ordinarily 4:00 p.m. E.S.T.) every day the New York Stock Exchange is open”; “If the NYSE closes early on a valuation day, the Funds shall determine NAV as of that time.”

requirements.text: For a FLEX Option with no same-day market trade, use the model-based price supplied by its exchange at the exchange's official close.
requirements.source: “FLEX Options listed on an exchange will typically be valued at a model-based price provided by the exchange at the official close of that exchange’s trading day.”

requirements.text: If a FLEX Option has a same-day market trading price, use that trade price instead of the exchange model price for all holdings of that option.
requirements.source: “When the Fund’s option has a same-day market trading price, this same-day market trading price will be used for FLEX Option values instead of the exchange’s model-based price.”

requirements.text: If the exchange cannot provide a model price and there is no applicable same-day trade price, use the backup third-party model price; if the required pricing vendor is unavailable, use the value determined by the Valuation Designee under the Valuation Procedures.
requirements.source: “If the exchange on which the option is traded is unable to provide a model price, model-based FLEX Options prices will additionally be provided by a backup third-party pricing provider”; “If either pricing vendor is not available to provide a model price for that day, the value of a FLEX option will be determined by Innovator as Valuation Designee in accordance with the Valuation Procedures.”

requirements.text: If the same FLEX Option is represented in both an all-cash basket and an in-kind basket on the same trading day, use the applicable trade price for both rather than a model price for the in-kind transaction.
requirements.source: “In instances where in the same trading day, a particular FLEX Option is represented in an all-cash basket…as well as in an in-kind basket…for valuation purposes that trading day the Fund will default to use the trade price for both instances.”

requirements.text: Calculate daily option unrealized gain or loss as current value less identified cost for purchased options and as premium received less the current liability for written options; transfer the applicable amount to realized gain or loss when a position is closed, expires, settles or is delivered in kind.
requirements.source: “The Trust determines the gain or loss realized from investment transactions on the basis of identified cost”; “If an option expires on the stipulated expiration date or if the Funds enter into a closing sale transaction, a gain or loss is realized.”

requirements.text: For a purchased option sold before expiration, record proceeds net of commissions and realize the difference between those proceeds and the identified cost of the contracts sold; do not calculate the realized result until the disposed tax/accounting lot has been identified when multiple lots exist.
requirements.source: “The Trust determines the gain or loss realized from investment transactions on the basis of identified cost.”

requirements.text: For a written option bought back before expiration, include brokerage commissions in the closing-purchase amount and realize premium allocated to the closed contracts minus that total closing amount; retain the allocated original premium for contracts still open.
requirements.source: “The difference between the premium and the amount paid on effecting a closing purchase transaction, including brokerage commissions, is also treated as a realized gain, or if the premium is less than the amount paid for the closing purchase transaction, as a realized loss.”

requirements.text: At expiration, cash-settle each call at max(reference closing price minus strike, zero) times the multiplier and contracts, and each put at max(strike minus reference closing price, zero) times the multiplier and contracts; record the amount as receivable for purchased options and payable for written options.
requirements.source: “The amount of cash is equal to the difference between the closing price of the Reference Asset’s price return and the exercise price of the option contract times a specified multiple.”

requirements.text: At expiration, set an out-of-the-money option to zero and realize the remaining purchased cost as a loss or the remaining written premium as a gain; for an in-the-money cash-settled option, realize settlement proceeds or obligations against its cost or premium.
requirements.source: “Option contracts that expire unexercised have no value”; “Premiums received from writing options that expire unexercised are treated…as realized gain from written options.”

requirements.text: After all prior-period FLEX Options cash-settle at the end of an Outcome Period, remove them from the books and record the new series of FLEX Options for the next Outcome Period on its trade date.
requirements.source: “Upon conclusion of the Outcome Period, the Fund will receive the cash value of all the FLEX Options it held for the prior Outcome Period. It will then invest in a new series of FLEX Options.”

requirements.text: Accrue the 0.79% annual unitary management fee daily based on average daily net assets, using the fund's configured day-count convention, and record it as a liability until paid monthly.
requirements.source: “pay monthly the Adviser a unitary fee calculated daily based on the average daily net assets…at the annual rate of 0.79%.”

requirements.text: Accrue interest on the money market deposit account for every calendar day, including intervening weekend days, using the applicable variable annual rate and configured day-count convention.
requirements.source: “The MMDA will bear interest at a variable rate that is determined based on market conditions and is subject to change daily”; “Interest income…is recognized on an accrual basis.”

requirements.text: Do not accrue dividend income merely because the reference ETF goes ex-dividend; recognize only the resulting mark-to-market changes in the price-return FLEX Options.
requirements.source: “The Cap and Buffer will be provided on a price return basis…and the Fund will not receive the benefit of any dividends.”

requirements.text: Process creations and redemptions only in Creation Units at the applicable daily NAV; increase or decrease shares outstanding by the shares in the accepted order and settle ordinarily on T+1.
requirements.source: “The Fund will issue or redeem its Shares at NAV per Share only in Creation Units”; “The delivery of Creation Units properly created will occur no later than…T+1”; “The requisite Cash Redemption Amount…will ordinarily be transferred no later than T+1.”

requirements.text: For an in-kind creation, calculate the Cash Component as NAV per Creation Unit minus the market value of the Deposit Instruments; for an in-kind redemption, calculate the Cash Redemption Amount as NAV per Creation Unit minus the market value of the instruments delivered.
requirements.source: “The Cash Component is an amount equal to the difference between the NAV of a Fund’s shares (per Creation Unit) and the Deposit Amount”; “Cash Redemption Amount…equal to the difference between the net asset value…per Creation Unit…and the aggregate market value of the Deposit Instruments.”

requirements.text: Where a pro-rata basket produces a fractional option contract, use the whole-contract quantity specified by the basket process and include the resulting difference from NAV in the balancing cash; minor deviations are permitted when an instrument cannot operationally be included pro rata.
requirements.source: “When utilizing a pro-rata basket, minor deviations may occur when it is not operationally feasible to include a particular instrument within the basket.”

requirements.text: Charge the stated creation or redemption transaction fee once per order regardless of the number of Creation Units, add a creation fee to the purchaser's payment, deduct a redemption fee from proceeds, and record a fee retained by the Fund as Transaction Fees.
requirements.source: “A transaction fee is applicable to each transaction regardless of the number of units purchased or sold in the transaction”; “Additional charges received by the Funds, if any, are disclosed as Transaction Fees.”

requirements.text: Treat options delivered in kind as disposals at their basket values and record the resulting identified-cost realized gain or loss in the applicable in-kind purchased-option or written-option category.
requirements.source: “Amount is included in realized gain/(loss) in-kind on the Statements of Operations.”

requirements.text: Process exchange or OCC corporate-action adjustments to contract quantity, strike, multiplier and deliverable together so that an economically neutral split does not change the option position's value solely because of the adjustment.

Calculate net assets as total marked assets, including cash and accrued income, less written-option liabilities, accrued management fees and all other liabilities; divide by shares outstanding and publish NAV per share rounded to the nearest cent.
requirements.source: “The NAV for one Share…is calculated by taking the market price of the Fund’s total assets, including any interest or dividends accrued but not yet collected, less all liabilities, and dividing such amount by the total number of Shares outstanding. The result, rounded to the nearest cent is the NAV per Share.”

requirements.text: Run daily price-staleness and NAV-error controls; calculate the corrected NAV using current prices, but obtain the correction and shareholder-compensation threshold from approved valuation or NAV-error procedures because the supplied public documents do not specify one.
